idea-plugin.name: MCP Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Adds code navigation, refactoring, quick fix, run control, module, diagnostics, build, file outline and history tools for AI agents to the IDE's built-in MCP Server.

MCP Companion complements the bundled MCP Server plugin, which must be enabled. Its tools appear next to the built-in ones for every MCP client connected to the IDE, and their names start with mc_. It does not duplicate built-in tools: when a newer IDE ships an official tool with the same capability, the matching MCP Companion tool steps aside by itself (checked at IDE start and when plugins are installed, updated or removed).

Tools

  • mc_find_usages: every reference to a symbol, in the project or also in libraries, with a read/write filter and paging.
  • mc_find_implementations: implementations, inheritors and overriding methods, or the supertypes and super methods.
  • mc_type_hierarchy: supertypes and subtypes of a class, with depth and size limits (JVM languages).
  • mc_safe_delete: preview lists what still uses a declaration; apply deletes it only when nothing does, as one undoable command.
  • mc_move: move a Java class to another package or source root with the IDE's Move refactoring, updating every reference in Java and Kotlin; preview first, applied only without conflicts.
  • mc_change_signature: add, remove, reorder, rename or retype a Java method's parameters, or change its return type or visibility, updating every call and overriding method; preview first, applied only without conflicts.
  • mc_run: start, stop and restart existing run configurations (run or debug), or run a test method, test class, test directory or main function directly from the code like the Run gutter icon, read the console output, wait until they are ready, hot-swap changed classes into a JVM debug session, and read test results (counts, failed tests with message and stack trace), also while the tests are running.
  • mc_modules: modules with their content roots and folders, the dependency graph with scopes (also as a Mermaid flowchart), and dependency cycles.
  • mc_diagnostics: errors and warnings of a module, a directory or a list of files, found by the IDE's own analysis without building, with line and column and totals per module.
  • mc_build: build one module with what it depends on, instead of the whole project, and get the errors with file, line and column, also when the build is delegated to Gradle or Maven.
  • mc_quick_fix: list the IDE's quick fixes for the problems of a file (add an import, add throws, make a class abstract, ...) and apply one as an undoable command, without opening the file; fixes that would ask for input are refused.
  • mc_file_structure: the outline of a file from the IDE's Structure view (classes, methods, fields, nested types with their lines), so that an agent reads only the part of a large file it needs.
  • mc_local_history: put a label in the IDE's Local History before a risky change, compare a file or directory with a label or a point in time, and revert to it as an undoable command.
  • mc_vcs_history: commit history of a file or of some of its lines, blame, and diffs between revisions or against the working copy, through the IDE's VCS integration.
  • mc_sync: re-import Gradle and Maven projects after build file changes and report the result.
  • mc_status: plugin version, IDE build and the state of each MCP Companion tool.

Safety

  • Before mc_run starts or restarts a process (also from code), the IDE asks you to allow or deny it, as the built-in execute_run_configuration does. Whether the IDE asks is the MCP Server's brave mode, which is off by default.
  • mc_run only runs run configurations of the project or the code of the project (as the IDE's temporary configurations), never arbitrary commands.
  • mc_safe_delete refuses to delete a declaration that is still used or that lies outside the project.
  • mc_move and mc_change_signature refuse to change code while the IDE reports conflicts; every change is one undoable command, as is each fix mc_quick_fix applies and each revert of mc_local_history.
  • mc_run, mc_sync and mc_build refuse to run anything in a project that is not trusted.

Settings

Switch individual tools on or off on the MCP Server's tool page. Settings | Tools | MCP Companion shows the state of each tool, links to that page, holds the brave mode setting and copies an optional guide for AI agents (for AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md) on how the tools work together. The user interface is available in English and Simplified Chinese.

Compatibility

Only the latest major IDE version is supported, currently 2026.3. When a new major version needs changes, a new plugin version follows; IDEs of earlier major versions keep the last plugin version that supports them.
